\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
The ALU that executed every add so far is one large combinational machine: many results computed at once, one chosen. Next: these circuits at work in the second part of Verm1.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item Combinational or sequential: an adder; a counter of button presses; a multiplexer; the processor as a whole? State the rule you used.
\item The ALU computes the sum, the AND, the OR, the XOR and a shift of the same two words at the same time. How does only the result of add t2, t0, t1 reach t2, and who chooses it?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
